Laura (Support): FYI Mariner (enterprise) reports 3x p95 on /generate-chat and /embeddings since last deploy (~02:10 UTC). Ticket INC-9876 created. Attaching a short trace and sampled latencies.

Laura (Support): sample p50: 180ms -> 540ms, p95: 420ms -> 1.3s after deploy. QPS steady ~120 for those routes.

Sam (Runtime): ack. Is this Hosted or Dedicated capacity for Mariner?

Laura (Support): Dedicated pool: mariner-prod-d1. Customer on reserved contract. No config changes reported on their side.

Jin (Eng-ML): any model/version changes in the last deploy? Quantized model swap or new kernel commit could cause fallback to slower path.

Rob (Infra): deploy-bot posted the deploy:```
deploy-bot: deploy mariner-prod @ 1975000600
 - service: runtime
 - image: runtime:release-2026-03-15
 - sha: a1b2c3d4
 - user: rob
```

Rob (Infra): that was the deploy-window that matches complaints.

Maya (Product): customer says they didn't change prompt shapes, but they did increase average context length slightly this week (from ~600 to ~900 tokens). Might matter.

Sam (Runtime): please grab kernel-selector logs and kv-cache metrics around 1975000600. Also want the exact pod id for one affected replica.

Laura (Support): pod id: mariner-runtime-7f6b9d4c8-xtzq2. Attached sample request IDs: req-33a, req-44b, req-77f.

Rob (Infra): running micro-bench on a replica now:```
$ rdw bench --model mariner-v2-q4f16 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --profile
decode p50: 200ms, decode p95: 900ms  (baseline last week p95 ~300ms)
cpu% shows high matmul time.```

Jin (Eng-ML): can you pull /var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log around the deploy? look for "fallback to matmul_fallback" or increased kernel cache misses. Those line markers correlate with slowed matmuls.

Rob (Infra): grabbing logs...```
1975000589 kernel-selector: selected fast_gemm for layer0
1975000598 kernel-selector: selected fast_gemm for layer1
1975000611 kernel-selector: fallback to matmul_fallback layer2 (quantized mismatch)
1975000613 kernel-selector: fallback to matmul_fallback layer3
1975000620 kernel-selector: cache miss for kernel fast_gemm
```

Jin (Eng-ML): there it is. fallback spikes at the same time as deploy. Likely kernel selector commit in runtime: the selector now aggressively invalidates kernel cache for slightly different tensor shapes; with longer contexts we hit a slow path.

Sam (Runtime): options: 1) back out selector commit (fast rollback), 2) flip selector config to be less strict, 3) temporary scale-up to absorb latency while we fix. Which do we prefer?

Kevin (SRE): quick mitigation -> scale pool by +30% and enable fallback policy that routes high-latency requests to mariner-v2-legacy (smaller context optimized). Customer ok?

Laura (Support): customer given go-ahead for temporary scale and canary rollback window this afternoon GMT; they want minimal user disruption.

Rob (Infra): scaling now: kubectl scale --replicas=13 deployment/mariner-prod-d1 (was 10). ops-bot created a scaling event.

ops-bot: Created incident follow-up ticket INC-9876-ops, scheduled canary rollback at 1975005400 UTC.

Sam (Runtime): I'll open a PR to revert the kernel-selector change and run canary rollback. Jin, can you validate regression locally and add a test?

Jin (Eng-ML): yes. I can repro with a sequence of mixed prompt lengths and the quantized build. Will instrument a micro-repro and run with/without selector change.

Rob (Infra): capturing perf on the replica:```
$ sudo perf record -e cpu-clock -p 12345 -g -- sleep 45
$ perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.fold
$ flamegraph.pl out.fold > flame.svg
Link: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/mariner/perf/1975001234/flame.svg
```

Sam (Runtime): looking at flamegraph — heavy stack in matmul_generic -> fallback_gemm_inner. Confirms selector fallback hits scalar path.

Jin (Eng-ML): root cause hypothesis: selector's shape-hash change makes quantized kernel lookup fail for padded shapes introduced by longer contexts. Fix: broaden shape buckets or fall back to nearest compatible kernel instead of invalidating.

Maya (Product): estimate for rollback -> Sam? And can we offer customer a short note that we're running a fix/canary rollback at X?

Sam (Runtime): rollback PR in 20m, canary to 2 pods in mariner-prod-d1 at 1975005400, monitor p95 and errors for 30m, then full rollout if green.

Laura (Support): I'll message the customer with the plan and ETA.

Kevin (SRE): after rollback, we'll keep an elevated autoscale buffer +30% for 2 hours, then revert. I put alert for p95>600ms.

Rob (Infra): uploaded kernel-selector.log snippet and bench output to INC-9876. Also saved the captured flame.svg for the team.

Sam (Runtime): Action items: Sam -> open rollback PR and coordinate canary; Jin -> validate fix & add regression test; Rob -> collect and hand off profiles/logs; Kevin -> scale + keep alerts; Laura -> customer comms.

Laura (Support): thanks all. I'll update the ticket and ping customer when canary starts. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Inc ticket INC-9876 updated: "canary rollback scheduled, mitigations applied, monitoring active"

Laura (Support): follow-up: will keep thread updates here and close when full rollout/confirmation done.
